column3: Self-administered microneedle patch for long-acting release of antiretroviral agents
column4: PROJECT NARRATIVEDespite the availability of antiviral drugs as treatment and prevention strategies for HIV there is still no cure andthere are ongoing challenges with adherence and delivery of current daily regimens. Our approach is to developa new slow-releasing formulation for highly potent antiviral drugs that will provide a novel delivery system usingbiodegradable microneedle patches that can be painlessly self-administered and can be used in adult andpediatric populations. This approach could provide a strategy for simplified long-term administration of antiviraldrugs for up to several months to increase medication adherence and treatment efficacy.

column3: DSP nanoparticles for treating nitrogen mustard induced corneal injury
column4: PROJECT NARRATIVEThe goal of this project is to evaluate a new method by the subconjunctival injection of DSP nanoparticles fortreating nitrogen mustard (NM)-induced corneal injury. Therapeutic interventions to treat NM-induced ocularinjury has not been identified yet which highlights the need to develop new treatment options for vesicants-induced corneal injury. The sustained releasing DSP-PLA-NP could be effective in preventing corneal NVcorneal ulceration corneal opacity suppressing inflammatory and angiogenic markers after NM exposure.

column4: Oral administration is considered a more favorable route of administration than injection because of improved convenience and compliance by patients resulting in improved treatment efficacy.
